chunks: Zurarah said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام:

A man joined a people in their salat (prayer) while not intending it as a salat of his own, and their Imam had become invalidated in purity, so he took that man's hand and brought him forward, and he led them in salat. Does their salat suffice for them by his salat while he did not intend it as a salat?

He said: 'It is not proper for a man to enter with a people in their salat while not intending it as a salat. Rather, he should intend it, and if he has already prayed, then he will have another salat. Otherwise, he should not enter with them. Yet the people's salat may still suffice for them even if he did not intend it.'

key_terms.أَتُجْزِيهِمْ: does it suffice and count as valid for them
key_terms.أَحْدَثَ: to incur a state that invalidates ritual purity during salat
key_terms.فَقَدَّمَهُ: he brought him forward to lead the congregation
key_terms.يَنْوِيهَا: to intend the prayer as one's own act of worship

ai.seo_question: Is congregational salat valid if a person who did not intend the prayer is brought forward to lead?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of joining congregational salat without intending it as one's own prayer, then being advanced to lead when the original Imam can no longer continue. Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام states that one should intend the salat upon joining, even if it becomes an additional prayer after already having prayed. At the same time, he indicates that the congregation's salat may still be valid even if the substitute leader had not made that intention.
